_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-19 18:38:48Z)**_

You don't have a sync bug here. Two different things in that log look like errors, and only one of them actually fails the run.

**1. `Error parsing sync request Error: illegal tag…` is expected.** It comes from the test `/sync > returns 500 if the request body is invalid`, which sends a deliberately broken body and checks that the server rejects it. That error gets logged and the test passes. All 50 files and 606 tests passed.

**2. `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink '…\test-server-files\account.sqlite'` is the real failure.** It happens after the tests finish, during the cleanup step:

- [vitest.globalSetup.js:102-104](packages/sync-server/vitest.globalSetup.js#L102-L104): the cleanup reverses all the setup migrations.
- The last one to be reversed, [1694360000000-create-folders.ts](packages/sync-server/migrations/1694360000000-create-folders.ts), deletes the `serverFiles` folder.
- But `account.sqlite` is still open. The setup step opened it through `getAccountDb()` in [account-db.js:17-24](packages/sync-server/src/account-db.js#L17-L24), and nothing ever closes it.
- Windows won't delete a file that's still open, so the delete fails with `EBUSY` and vitest marks the package as failed. Linux and macOS do allow deleting open files, which is why this only shows up on your machine and not in CI.

Your repo path having spaces has nothing to do with it.

**Fix:** close the database before deleting the folder. Add a small helper to [account-db.js](packages/sync-server/src/account-db.js):

```js
export function closeAccountDb() {
  if (_accountDb !== undefined) {
    _accountDb.close();
    _accountDb = undefined;
  }
}
```

Then call it at the start of `down` in `1694360000000-create-folders.ts`, before the `fs.rm` calls:

```ts
export const down = async function (): Promise<void> {
  closeAccountDb();
  await fs.rm(config.get('serverFiles'), { recursive: true, force: true });
  await fs.rm(config.get('userFiles'), { recursive: true, force: true });
};
```

I'd put it in the migration rather than the test cleanup because a real `down` migration on Windows would hit the same error. Setting `_accountDb` back to `undefined` means anything that calls `getAccountDb()` later gets a fresh connection instead of a closed one.

I haven't made this change or run anything yet. Want me to apply it and run the sync-server tests to confirm the `EBUSY` is gone?

Until then, a run that fails only with this `EBUSY` doesn't mean any tests failed. You may also need to delete the leftover `packages/sync-server/test-server-files/` folder by hand before the next run, since the cleanup didn't finish.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-19 19:18:36Z)**_

Run this from the repo root:

```bash
yarn test:debug
```

It's defined in the root `package.json` as `lage test --no-cache --continue`. That runs every package's tests and ignores lage's saved results, so nothing gets marked `skipped` the way most packages were in your earlier output.

**Other options:**

- **Delete the cache, then run normally:** `rm -rf .lage` in Git Bash, or `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .lage` in PowerShell, followed by `yarn test`. After that, later `yarn test` runs start caching again.
- **Test a single package:** `yarn workspace @actual-app/sync-server run test`. This runs vitest directly without going through lage, so lage's cache doesn't apply.

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.

Written for: the reviewers of this PR, as sections to paste into its description.

```markdown
## Tech Debt

**Introduced**

- `account-db.js` is still plain JavaScript, so the new `closeAccountDb()` helper is untyped.
- The `create-folders` down migration now depends on `account-db.js`. Before, it only deleted folders.

**Encountered**

- The shared account database connection is never closed anywhere else, including when the server shuts down.
- If the test cleanup fails, it leaves stale files behind (`.migrate-test` and `test-server-files/`). They have to be deleted by hand before the tests will run again.
- Tests that are expected to fail log real-looking errors (`Error parsing sync request`, `Invalid Origin header`), which makes the test output hard to read.

## Design Decisions

- **The database is closed in the migration, not the test cleanup.** A real down migration on Windows would hit the same `EBUSY` error, so fixing it in the migration covers both cases.
- **The connection is reset after it's closed.** `closeAccountDb()` clears the stored connection, so the next `getAccountDb()` call opens a fresh one instead of reusing a closed one.
- **The change is kept small.** No test files or shared database code were changed. Only the database that blocks the folder delete gets closed.
```

Written for: the reviewers of this PR, as the description section. It covers the whole branch, including your earlier commit.

```markdown
## Description

Fixes test failures that show up when running `yarn test` locally, especially on Windows (#98, #94).

- **sync-server:** Test cleanup failed with `EBUSY` because `account.sqlite` was still open when the folder holding it was deleted. The down migration now closes the account database first.
- **loot-core `main.test.ts`:** Each test now closes the budget before deleting its files, for the same Windows reason.
- **loot-core `vitest.config.ts`:** Vitest now skips the copies of test files inside Stryker's `.stryker-tmp/` folder, and keeps its default exclude list.
- **desktop-client `mutations.test.tsx`:** The test now waits for i18next to finish starting up before rendering. Otherwise the hook could return `null` after running `yarn generate:i18n`.

All tests pass on Windows with no cleanup errors.
```

If this PR only fixes some of #98 and #94, change "Fixes" to "Addresses" so GitHub doesn't treat them as resolved.
